description: Eight-bit shift register after Rob Hordijk's Benjolin and Blippoo Box, with a stepped voltage built from the last three bits

params.text: Sets the voltage the Data input is compared against, -5V to +5V; a data voltage above it writes a one into the first bit
Attenuverts the CV that shifts the comparison voltage, -1 to +1, and zero at startup, so that input does nothing until this is turned up
Scales the stepped output, -5V to +5V, inverting it below zero
Attenuverts the CV that shifts the output scaling, -1 to +1, and zero at startup, so that input does nothing until this is turned up
Write feeds the Data input into the register; Loop ignores Data and fills the first bit from the last bit alone, so the pattern repeats unchanged
Direct fills the first bit from the Data comparison alone; XOR fills it from that comparison exclusive-ORed with the last bit, which is far less predictable

inputs.text: A rising edge advances the register by one bit
Compared against the comparison voltage; above it a one enters the register, below it a zero
Shifts the comparison voltage, through its own attenuverter
Shifts the output scaling, through its own attenuverter

outputs.text: 5V while that bit of the register holds a one, 0V while it holds a zero
The stepped voltage built from the last three bits of the register, eight levels between 0V and the level set by the Scale knob

notes: the register starts with every bit at zero and stays there while Data is unpatched and Compare is at 0V; a clock on its own changes nothing until Data rises above the Compare voltage.
